The as-cast Ti–Zr–Nb–V alloy ingots was prepared by vacuum arc melting from raw metals with a purity of > 99.9% in a high-purity argon atmosphere.
The ingot was remelted at least 6 times to achieve a homogeneous distribution of the constituent elements.
The samples used for the subsequent characterization measurements were cut from the ingot by electrical discharge machining.

conflicts.description: The reported compression yield strength of V30 and V35 contradicts the stated increase of yield strength with increasing V/Zr ratio, as V30 and V35 have the same value of 1010 MPa.

The text states that the yield strength of Ti–Zr–Nb–V alloys increases with increasing V/Zr ratio, but the compression data shows a slight decrease from V25 (969 MPa) to V30 (1010 MPa) and V35 (1010 MPa) remains same as V30.
